summary: Extends the RTP payload format of RFC 3640 to carry MPEG Surround multi-channel audio. It defines extra media type parameters for signaling backward-compatible transmission inside an MPEG-4 Audio stream, and also describes layered transmission. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: Surround sound uses many speakers. This document says how to send that sound over the Internet so an older player hears normal stereo and a newer player gets the full surround effect.

questions: rtp payload format for mpeg surround
how to carry multi-channel audio in rtp
how to carry mpeg surround in rtp
subtitle: How to send surround-sound audio over RTP so that old stereo players still work and new ones get all the channels.

tldr.problem: MPEG Surround rebuilds many audio channels from a mono or stereo downmix plus a small amount of control data, but RFC 3640 did not say how to carry that data over RTP or how to signal it.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lets the surround data ride inside the downmix AAC stream as an extension that old decoders skip, or travel as its own elementary stream in two new modes, MPS-lbr and MPS-hbr, tied to the downmix stream by SDP.
tldr.outcome: Existing stereo services can be upgraded to surround in a backwards-compatible way. The RFC is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3640.

today: RFC 5691 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2009 that updates RFC 3640. The unit metadata shows no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why MPEG Surround Needs a Payload Format
sections.content:
MPEG Surround (Spatial Audio Coding) is an international standard finalized by MPEG in January 2007. It can re-create N channels from M < N transmitted channels plus additional control data. The M channels are usually a single mono channel or a stereo pair.

For 5.1 audio, the encoder makes a stereo or mono downmix and a compact description of the full 5.1 material. The control data takes far less bandwidth than sending every channel. A legacy stereo decoder ignores it and plays the stereo signal with no quality loss, while a surround-enabled decoder produces multi-channel audio.

This RFC extends the RTP payload format of RFC 3640 to carry this data and adds media type parameters to signal it.
sections.plainLanguage: Imagine a song recorded for many speakers, plus a small note saying how to spread it out. Plain players use the simple version and ignore the note. Fancy players use the note to fill the room.

sections.title: Configuration and Frames
sections.content:
The RFC splits MPEG Surround data into two parts. The SpatialSpecificConfig() (SSC) holds configuration. The SpatialFrame() holds the actual surround payload.

The configuration can be sent in-band, where the SSC travels in a SacDataFrame() together with a SpatialFrame(). It can also be sent out-of-band, for example with the Session Description Protocol (RFC 4566). An AudioSpecificConfig() with an audioObjectType of 30 contains an SSC.

Spatial frames can be embedded in the downmix stream or sent as separate elementary streams next to it. The AAC decoder buffer limits the size of an Access Unit, so for high-bitrate uses that exceed the limit, all MPEG Surround data MUST go in a separate stream.
sections.plainLanguage: There are two kinds of pieces: a setup sheet that says how things are arranged, and the sound pieces themselves. The setup sheet can ride along with the sound or be handed over separately.

sections.title: Embedding Surround Data in AAC
sections.content:
MPEG-4 Audio lets extra data ride inside AAC payloads as an extension_payload(). MPEG Surround data uses the type EXT_SAC_DATA. Because AAC decoders are required to skip unknown extension data, the result is a single stream that older decoders handle unchanged. It is transported as specified in RFC 3640.

No new mode is introduced here. Either AAC-lbr or AAC-hbr SHOULD be used, and the new MPS-profile-level-id and MPS-config parameters SHOULD be present. Any SSC inside a SacDataFrame() MUST be identical to the SSC conveyed through SDP for that stream.

The RFC gives an SDP example with mode=AAC-hbr in which the downmix is HE AAC Profile at Level 2 (PLI 44) and the surround part is MPEG Surround Baseline Profile at Level 3 (PLI 55).
sections.plainLanguage: The surround note is tucked inside the normal audio like a small envelope inside a package. Old players do not open envelopes they do not know, so they just play the music.

sections.title: A Separate Surround Stream
sections.content:
The spatial frames can instead form their own elementary stream that complements the downmix stream. The downmix can use any coding scheme. The mode for this stream MUST be MPS-hbr or MPS-lbr, and MPS-hbr SHALL be used when a frame may exceed 63 bytes.

The two streams are linked with the dependency signaling of RFC 5583. Their media clocks SHALL be in the same clock domain and MUST NOT drift, and the sampling rate of the surround signal and the decoded downmix MUST be identical. Because separate RTP streams have different random timestamp offsets, RTCP MUST be used to synchronize them. RTCP sender reports MUST indicate that the timestamps are not drifting.

If HE AAC is the downmix coder, the downmix RTP clock rate MAY be the sampling rate of the AAC core.
sections.plainLanguage: Here the surround note travels in its own envelope next to the music. Both must use the same clock so they line up, like two runners keeping exactly the same pace.

sections.title: The Low and High Bitrate Modes
sections.content:
MPS-lbr carries one or more complete Access Units, each a single SpatialFrame() of at most 63 bytes. Fragmentation MUST NOT be used. Its 1-octet AU header gives the frame size in 6 bits and 2 bits of index information. The parameters sizeLength, indexLength and indexDeltaLength MUST be present with fixed values 6, 2 and 2.

MPS-hbr carries one fragment of an Access Unit, one complete one, or several complete ones, with a SpatialFrame() of at most 8191 bytes. Its 2-octet AU header gives the size in 13 bits and 3 bits of index information, and the fixed values are 13, 3 and 3. Each AU-Index field MUST be coded as 0.

In both modes the Auxiliary Section MUST be empty, receivers MUST support de-interleaving, maxDisplacement MUST be present when interleaving, and constantDuration MUST signal the fixed duration. The config value is the hexadecimal ASC with an object type of 30 and sacPayloadEmbedding set to 0.
sections.plainLanguage: There is a small-box mode and a big-box mode. Small boxes hold tiny pieces and can never be split. Big boxes hold bigger pieces and may be split across several packets.

sections.title: Media Type Parameters and Modes
sections.content:
The RFC adds optional parameters to the audio/mpeg4-generic media type. They SHALL be used when MPEG Surround data is inside an AAC elementary stream, and only with the AAC-lbr or AAC-hbr modes.

  • MPS-profile-level-id: a decimal MPEG Surround Profile and Level indication, used in capability exchange or session set-up to say what the decoder must be able to handle.
  • MPS-config: a hexadecimal ASC for MPEG Surround. Its object type SHALL be 30 and its SSC MUST have sacPayloadEmbedding set to 1.

It also registers the MPS-hbr and MPS-lbr values for the mode parameter. The two new parameters SHALL NOT be used with those two modes. The media format parameters are assumed to be conveyed in SDP as described in RFC 3640.
sections.plainLanguage: The document adds new labels to the official list so everyone writes the same words on the box. Some labels go with one box type and must never be mixed with the other.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
These packets inherit the security considerations of the RTP specification (RFC 3550) and of RFC 3640. The main concerns are confidentiality, integrity and source authenticity. The right mechanism depends on the application, transport and signaling, but SRTP (RFC 3711) is recommended if suitable. IPsec and TLS are also mentioned.

The RFC adds one specific warning. The AAC extension mechanism is gracefully skipped by decoders that do not understand it, and this covert channel may be used to transmit unauthorized data in an otherwise valid stream.
sections.plainLanguage: Because old players ignore the hidden envelope, someone could sneak a secret message in it. The document warns about that and suggests locking the whole package with encryption.
